profile.prompt: What has been taking up the most room in your head lately?

options.text: Friends and where I fit
Work, school, or what comes next
Dating or family stuff
My routines, energy, or body
Something else, or I can't name it yet

profile.contextNote: Route only. Route tags never become personality evidence.
profile.claimLimit: A selected topic is not a diagnosis, trait, or proof of a problem.

profile.prompt: Which sounds closest to your social life these days?

options.text: I see people often and feel known by at least a few
I see people often, but still edit parts of myself
I have a small circle and that mostly suits me
My people-time has been changing lately
None of these quite fits

profile.contextNote: Present-day context only; do not universalize to every relationship.
profile.claimLimit: Does not establish loneliness, belonging insecurity, or relationship quality.

profile.prompt: If this chat got one thing right about you, what would you want it to help with?

options.text: Help me understand a pattern I keep repeating
Help me put words to what I feel
Help me decide what to do next
Give me a funny, weirdly accurate read
I don't have a specific goal

profile.contextNote: Preference signal only, never a scored trait.
profile.claimLimit: A desired kind of help is not evidence that the person needs or received it.

profile.prompt: Optional, and you can keep it broad: is there something you feel a bit tender or unsure about lately?

options.text: How I come across to people
Whether I am doing enough or keeping up
A choice or goal I care about
Something else
I'd rather not say, or nothing comes to mind

profile.contextNote: Explicit, optional private context. Never a score, public label, or prerequisite; no follow-up unless participant opts in.
profile.claimLimit: Do not infer universal insecurity, pathology, or a stable self-esteem trait.

profile.prompt: Would you want an optional feature where you invite one chosen friend to guess or gently challenge one of your reads? Nothing would be shared unless you chose to invite them.

options.text: Yes, that sounds fun
Maybe, after I see my own read
No, keep this just for me
Not sure yet

profile.contextNote: Feature preference only; this response is not consent to contact a friend or share any data. A separate explicit action would be required if such a feature existed.
profile.claimLimit: Does not establish relationship trust or sharing consent.

profile.prompt: If Genii checks whether a read fits, what approach would feel right to you?

options.text: Ask gently and keep it brief
Be direct; I can handle a clean edit
Keep it playful, but let me say what missed
Ask permission before opening feedback

profile.contextNote: Interaction preference only. Any later fit feedback remains separate from profile evidence and is requested with permission.
profile.claimLimit: Does not establish agreement, disagreement, or current fit of any interpretation.

profile.prompt: Think of the latest social invitation this past month where the occasion's purpose and your own excitement didn't quite match. The group chat had opinions. What did you actually do?

options.text: Went because I was excited about it
Went because the occasion or its purpose mattered
Went mainly to be with the people
Suggested a different way to take part
Passed and let them know

profile.contextNote: Actual report; retain event purpose and attendance. Follow-up n08 applies only when n07 has an authored event/action response.
profile.claimLimit: Purpose and enjoyment are separate; neither attendance nor refusal establishes sociability, selfishness, or people-pleasing.

profile.prompt: What mattered most in that choice?

options.text: I was looking forward to it
I cared about the occasion's purpose
I wanted time with those people
My time, energy, or other plans decided it
Avoiding tension mattered most
Something else

profile.contextNote: Ask only after an authored n07 response. Skip for Other, Skip, no-example, or omission; do not assume the person attended.
profile.claimLimit: Direct motive report for one event, not a hidden motive diagnosis.

profile.prompt: A close friend asks you to come along to a low-key thing. You like them, but the event itself is not your scene. What's your move?

options.text: Go; the friend is the good part
Suggest something we'd both enjoy
Pass kindly; liking them doesn't make every plan my plan
Ask what they need from me before deciding

profile.contextNote: Hypothetical intention, distinct from reported behavior.
profile.claimLimit: Does not establish what the respondent does in real events.

profile.prompt: Same low-key event, but the person asking is someone you know only a little. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Go; trying the event sounds fine
Ask for details, then decide
Suggest another way to hang out
Pass; the event isn't for me

profile.contextNote: Paired with n09 to preserve relationship-target contrast. Intended choice only.
profile.claimLimit: Difference from n09 may reflect event comfort, not a global closeness trait.

profile.prompt: In the past month, think of a recent moment when you contributed to something other people would notice. What did you most want from it?

options.text: The thing itself going well
People knowing I helped
A chance to show what I can do
I wasn't looking for anything in particular

profile.contextNote: Self-reported motive about a recent contribution; select no-example if none.
profile.claimLimit: Wanting credit or visibility is not proof of insecurity, vanity, or narcissism.

profile.prompt: Think of a recent time this month someone around you got praise for something you also care about. Your inner scoreboard might wake up. What did you actually do next?

options.text: Congratulated them
Asked how they got the opportunity
Made my own contribution visible
Returned to what I was working on

profile.contextNote: Action-only response; any feeling or comparison thought is not measured by this item.
profile.claimLimit: A single action does not imply envy, competitiveness, or insecurity.

profile.prompt: Think of feedback you received this month that, after considering it, you felt had a fair point. The notes app is open. What did you do first?

options.text: Asked what they meant or for an example
Explained my side, then considered their point
Took time before responding
Looked for one part I could use

profile.contextNote: Concern is follow-through on feedback the respondent considers credible, not reaction to disrespect. Keep source and whether it felt fair. No-example uses sentinel if none.
profile.claimLimit: Does not measure openness, resilience, or establish that every criticism was accurate.

profile.prompt: In the past month, was there a moment you realized something you said or did landed badly with someone? What happened next? The tiny repair department is open.

options.text: I checked in and tried to make it right
I explained what I meant
I gave them space and came back later
I wasn't sure what to do

profile.contextNote: No-example is a separate sentinel from authored choices and Skip. Ask only about recognized impact; do not assume harm.
profile.claimLimit: A single repair episode does not establish empathy, fault, or relationship outcome.

profile.prompt: Think of a recent time this month a particular person's reply mattered to you and took longer than you'd hoped. What did you actually do while waiting? You do not need to name them.

options.text: Sent one follow-up message
Waited without checking the chat
Checked the chat or their status
Couldn't tell what I did

profile.contextNote: Target-specific actual event; no assumption that every delayed reply is meaningful. Use no-example sentinel when no person/recent instance fits.
profile.claimLimit: A wait response alone does not imply attachment style, rejection fear, or the other person's intent.

profile.prompt: In the past month, when you wanted something from a person whose opinion mattered to you, how did you let them know?

options.text: Said what I wanted plainly
Hinted or waited to see if they'd notice
Tried to handle it myself
Decided it wasn't worth bringing up

profile.contextNote: Keep the target and recent situation available for interpretation.
profile.claimLimit: Does not establish a universal communication style or the reason for withholding.

profile.prompt: Think of the latest time someone offered you practical help this month. Did you take the assist?

options.text: Accepted it
Accepted after talking through the details
Declined and handled it myself
Declined but asked for a different kind of support

profile.contextNote: Actual event, no assumption that help was needed or that refusal was pride. Use no-example sentinel if no offer occurred.
profile.claimLimit: One response does not show dependency, independence, or comfort with all help.

profile.prompt: After a recent awkward conversation this month, once you had said your piece, what happened next for you?

options.text: We talked again and understood each other better
I took time away from the conversation
I talked it through with someone else
I focused on another activity
I kept turning it over in my head

profile.contextNote: Conditional on a recent awkward conversation and having said something; otherwise skip/no-example.
profile.claimLimit: Does not establish emotional regulation or recovery time unless directly measured elsewhere.

profile.prompt: In the past month, think of a request for help that competed with your time or energy. Your calendar is a witness. What did you do?

options.text: Helped, even though it squeezed my own plan
Helped in a smaller way I could manage
Offered another time or person
Said no

profile.contextNote: Actual trade-off, target retained; note urgency and available capacity where known. Choices carry no virtue order. Use no-example sentinel if no request fits.
profile.claimLimit: Saying no is not selfishness; saying yes is not proof of generosity or coercion.

profile.prompt: What mattered most in that choice, whether you helped or not?

options.text: I wanted to help that person
It felt like the right thing to do
My available time or energy set the limit
I felt pressure or found it hard to refuse
Something else

profile.contextNote: Ask only after an authored n19 response. Skip for Other, Skip, no-example, or omission; motive may be capacity even when the response was no.
profile.claimLimit: Directly reported motive for one event; not a moral judgment.

profile.prompt: For a shared plan or task you cared about this month, what role did you actually take?

options.text: Set the plan and kept track of the pieces
Took one piece and let others handle theirs
Asked what others wanted before choosing a role
Stayed flexible and adjusted as we went

profile.contextNote: Actual role, not hypothetical preference. Use no-example sentinel if no shared plan/task fits.
profile.claimLimit: Organizing does not imply controlling; adapting does not imply passivity.

profile.prompt: If that plan changed, what did you do first when you found out?

options.text: Worked out the new details
Said what part was frustrating or inconvenient
Went with it and adjusted on the fly
Asked to keep the original plan
The plan didn't change

profile.contextNote: Context follow-up only when the n21 plan changed; otherwise use the explicit no-change option. Skip for Other, Skip, no-example, or omission.
profile.claimLimit: One changed plan does not establish rigidity or flexibility as a trait.

profile.prompt: Think of a recent moment this month you felt irritated with someone. What did you show on the outside?

options.text: I said I was irritated
I stayed polite and dealt with it later
It came out in my tone or actions
I stepped away

profile.contextNote: Only outward action here; n24 separately asks about the felt experience. No-example remains distinct from authored options and Skip.
profile.claimLimit: A quiet exterior is not evidence of low intensity or calmness.

profile.prompt: How strong did the irritation feel inside at the time?

options.text: A small flicker
Noticeable, but manageable
Strong; it took up real space
Hard to tell now

profile.contextNote: Ask only if n23 references an actual event; skip for Other, Skip, no-example, or omission.
profile.claimLimit: Retrospective self-rating for one event, not a stable emotional-intensity scale.

profile.prompt: This month, when a decision felt uncertain but reversible, what did you actually do?

options.text: Picked a direction and tried it
Got one or two more details first
Asked someone I trust what they thought
Waited until it felt clearer

profile.contextNote: Scope is a reversible decision; do not generalize to major or high-risk choices.
profile.claimLimit: Does not establish decisiveness, anxiety, or control in other stakes.

profile.prompt: Think of a goal you cared about that felt behind schedule this month. Your calendar has entered the chat. What was your next move?

options.text: Made the next step smaller
Put in extra time to catch up
Changed the plan or deadline
Paused to figure out what was getting in the way

profile.contextNote: A missed or delayed goal is not presumed to be failure; no-example is a separate sentinel, not an authored option.
profile.claimLimit: Does not establish motivation or ability from one goal episode.

profile.prompt: Over the past month, how often did your usual sleep leave you feeling restored when you woke up?

options.text: Most mornings
Some mornings
Not often
It varied too much to say

profile.contextNote: Direct subjective routine anchor; ordinal wording is not a sleep-quality score.
profile.claimLimit: Do not infer duration, adequacy, cause, or medical status.

profile.prompt: And over just the last seven days, how often did sleep leave you feeling restored when you woke up?

options.text: Most mornings
Some mornings
Not often
It varied too much to say

profile.contextNote: Pair with n27; usual and recent remain separate reports, not a trend claim.
profile.claimLimit: No sleep cause, duration, or clinical conclusion.

profile.prompt: Over the past month, how steady was your usual meal timing from day to day?

options.text: Mostly steady
Some days steady, some not
Often shifted around
My days varied too much for a usual pattern

profile.contextNote: Direct meal-timing report only, not meal amount or nutrition quality.
profile.claimLimit: Do not infer eating disorder, adequacy, body state, or health cause.

profile.prompt: And over just the last seven days, how steady was your meal timing from day to day?

options.text: Mostly steady
Some days steady, some not
Often shifted around
My days varied too much for a usual pattern

profile.contextNote: Pair with n29; descriptive contrast only.
profile.claimLimit: No diet-quality, adequacy, medical, or causal claim.

profile.prompt: Over the past month, how often did you have enough energy for the things you wanted or needed to do?

options.text: Most days
Some days
Not often
It depended too much on the day to say

profile.contextNote: Direct subjective report of energy, not performance or cause.
profile.claimLimit: No medical, sleep, nutrition, or mental-health cause inferred.

profile.prompt: And over just the last seven days, how often did you have enough energy for the things you wanted or needed to do?

options.text: Most days
Some days
Not often
It depended too much on the day to say

profile.contextNote: Pair with n31; not a validated measure or a diagnosis.
profile.claimLimit: No medical, sleep, nutrition, or mental-health cause inferred.

checks.prompt: Your group has already picked a restaurant you don't care about, but you'd enjoy the company. What's your likeliest move?

options.text: Go for the people
Suggest a place I'd also enjoy
Join for part of it
Skip this one

checks.contextNote: Freeze any prediction before showing or recording this answer. Same target and social-purpose-versus-enjoyment dimension; hypothetical check, not profile evidence.
checks.claimLimit: No inference about actual event behavior; check answer must not update the frozen profile.

checks.prompt: A close friend is nervous about giving a short talk and asks you to sit in the audience. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Go to support them
Help them practice another way
Ask what kind of support would help
Say I can't make it

checks.contextNote: Near-transfer check for close-friend accompaniment in a support task rather than social outing. Freeze prediction first.
checks.claimLimit: Held out from profile; one hypothetical answer is not validated prediction accuracy.

checks.prompt: A teammate gets public credit for work you also helped with. What would you most likely do next?

options.text: Let the moment pass
Mention my part in the work
Congratulate them, then talk privately about credit
Focus on the next task

checks.contextNote: Same recognition/comparison family and peer target; scenario and action differ from n11/n12. Freeze first.
checks.claimLimit: Does not reveal motive, insecurity, or fairness of the situation.

checks.prompt: A reviewer points out a concrete flaw in a draft you care about. What's your first move?

options.text: Ask for a specific example
Explain what I was aiming for
Take a beat before answering
Mark what I would revise

checks.contextNote: Near-transfer hypothetical for follow-through on credible feedback; freeze prediction first.
checks.claimLimit: Hypothetical intent only; heldout answer never enters profile evidence.

checks.prompt: You notice a joke you made left someone quieter than before. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Check in with them
Explain that I meant it playfully
Give them room, then follow up
Wait to see if they bring it up

checks.contextNote: Same repair facet and affected-person target as n14, but hypothetical scenario. Freeze first.
checks.claimLimit: Does not establish actual repair or the impact of a real interaction.

checks.prompt: Someone whose reply matters has not answered your invitation to meet this weekend. What would you most likely do next?

options.text: Send one follow-up
Wait without checking the chat
Check the chat or their status
Decide later; I'm not sure

checks.contextNote: Near-transfer check for waiting on a chosen person's reply; does not combine asking for a need. Freeze first.
checks.claimLimit: Does not infer rejection fear or the other person's intention.

checks.prompt: A trusted friend offers to pick up one errand for you this week. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Accept the offer
Say what kind of help would fit
Thank them and handle it myself
Ask if we can revisit it later

checks.contextNote: Near-transfer hypothetical for receiving help; no added recovery/awkward-conversation bundle. Freeze first.
checks.claimLimit: Does not imply dependence, refusal discomfort, or actual recovery.

checks.prompt: A friend asks you to help them move a shelf tonight, but you had planned a quiet evening. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Help tonight
Offer a smaller bit of help
Suggest another time
Say I can't tonight

checks.contextNote: Near-transfer hypothetical for a helping boundary; motive is not embedded in choice. Freeze first.
checks.claimLimit: One intended choice cannot establish selfishness, generosity, or a stable boundary style.
